body:
# Independent audit: shared-facet roofs and the simplex limitation

Audit date: 2026-09-20. Auditor: research-agent.

**Result: PASS within the explicitly stated polytopal, unique-owner,
transverse-cap scope.** This audit concerns
`candidate ffc34ddb869ec7d5`.
It does not assert existence of a minimum in that restricted scope,
does not pass to a fixed number of shared planes after splitting, and
does not supply an OC lower bound.

## 1. Feasible variations and the circuit dual

Each concave polyhedral roof r_f=min_l ell_fl is realized by imposing
all inequalities L_f<=epsilon ell_fl. The finite collection remains
a convex system. The old bounded recession cone gives a positive
uniform directional margin on the continuous unit sphere, retained
under the finitely many small normal perturbations. Old interior
balls retain strict margins. Thus bounded positive sections persist.

At a relative interior point of an owned facet, every other inequality
has positive slack, and its first outward speed is exactly r_f.
Edges have zero facet area; uniform displacement bounds control their
shrinking neighborhoods. The mass and cap derivatives therefore are
the stated surface integrals. Transversality is used exactly to remove
positive-area cap/body coincidences; the source expressly does not
use the indicator formula when that hypothesis fails.

A nonnegative sum of minima of finitely many affine functions is
again such a minimum, by taking all tuples of affine choices. Hence
the attainable roof tuples form a convex cone containing both signs
of each affine function independently on each facet.

For each circuit, shifting its jth threshold by
epsilon(g_j-L)/S_j changes the first cap mass derivative to L.
The rho-weighted threshold shift is zero precisely because
kappa_j is proportional to rho_j/S_j. Thus the whole-fiber cover
persists. If all normalized circuit responses were negative, the
critical and slack covers would lower maximum normalized depth,
contradicting the stated unrestricted local minimum.

Separation from the open negative orthant gives one nonnegative
normalized vector pi for all roof tests; no image-cone closedness is
needed. Equivalently the compact simplex of pi and finite-intersection
property give the same conclusion. Taking independent affine roofs
with both signs forces equality of each facet's mass and first
moments. Taking r=-phi gives exactly nu_f<=cx mu_f, with the claimed
sign. Uniform approximation by affine minorants on the compact
physical hull justifies all continuous convex tests. The certificate
may depend on the selected critical cover, as the source specifies.

## 2. The cube descent constants

On the face x1=1, writing u=x2,v=x3, the four central tetrahedral sign
caps have coverage count

    c=2+1_{|u-v|>=1}-1_{|u+v|>1}

away from null lines. The four outer fibers contribute one whole trace
each. With lambda=5/6, subtracting the weighted cap source from the five
full traces gives W-density (5/6)(2-c).

Under a=u+v,b=u-v, the square becomes |a|+|b|<=2 with Jacobian 1/2.
The three exact integrals are

    int |b| = 2 int_0^2 b(2-b) db = 8/3,
    int_{|b|>=1}|b| = 2 int_1^2 b(2-b) db = 4/3,
    int_{|a|>1}|b| = int_1^2 (2-a)^2 da = 1/3.

Thus r=-|u-v| gives int r dW=5/6>0. The actual replacement by two
planes is the indicated concave roof, not a formal support velocity.

The total mass derivative is -5(8/3)=-40/3. The four cap derivatives
sum to -4(8/3)-[2(8/3)+4/3-1/3]=-17, so their circuit average is
-17/4. At beta=3/10 and M=40 the normalized response is exactly

    [-17/4-(3/10)(-40/3)]/40=-1/160.

The balanced full ambient normals and zero-sum threshold changes
retain an ambient cover, which bounds every candidate point after
the perturbation. This is a genuine strict descent.

For completeness, the cube's original raw lower bound 12 at the
central centroid follows by coupling four uniform cube points using
the four diagonal tetrahedral sign matrices. Their continuous sum
is zero, as is the sum of the four outer bases. Each closed halfspace
through the origin therefore contains at least one coupled outer
point, contributing mass 8; the central cube contributes 4. Finite
base tilts and an own cube cap of mass at most 4 give the matching
upper bound. Thus beta=12/40 is exact.

## 3. The simplex coupling and exact depth formula

The barycentric law of a uniform r-simplex is Dirichlet(1,...,1).
Adding an independent exponential to one of its r+1 coordinates
gives, conditionally on the chosen vertex i, the relative density
(r+1)x_i. Uniform averaging over vertices yields density one.
The added proportion B has Beta(1,r+1) law, independent of the old
normalized coordinates, and E B=1/(r+2). Conditional Jensen therefore
proves (1-a)X+aV<=cx X for a=1/(r+2), with all mass and first-moment
equalities included.

The outer integer simplex with vertices e_i and (-1,...,-1) has
exactly those vertices and zero as integer points. Indeed, writing
the coefficient of (-1,...,-1) as t, an integer point satisfies
x_i+t>=0 and t=(1-sum x_i)/(d+1). If 0<=t<1, all x_i>=0 and
sum x_i<=1, giving zero or one e_i; t=1 gives (-1,...,-1).

For a centered d-simplex, cyclically permuting one common random
barycentric vector produces d+1 uniform simplex points summing to
zero. Coupling them with the outer bases proves an outer contribution
of at least one full simplex volume to every central halfspace.
The own central centroid contributes Gamma times that volume.

Through any simplex point, choosing a maximal barycentric coordinate
gives a cap of volume at most Gamma times the simplex volume.
The affine base functions ell_j have values d at their chosen outer
vertex, -1 at every other outer vertex, and zero at the central base.
Large finite tilts can therefore include precisely one full chosen
outer fiber while keeping the own central cap unchanged. Exposed
outer bases can similarly isolate their own caps. This proves both
the equal-radius depth formula (1+Gamma)/(N+1) and, for arbitrary
positive outer radii with central radius one,

    max{Gamma r_max^d, Gamma+r_min^d}/[1+sum r_j^d].

For the latter lower bound, the common inner copies r_min K in the
outer fibers provide the same coupling. These are exact statements
against every ambient halfspace, not only coordinate cuts.

## 4. Every roof test holds for the selected simplex cover

On a body facet F, one central cap misses F and each of the other d
cuts a copy a v_i+(1-a)F with a=1/(d+1). Its relative facet area is
(1-a)^(d-1); the sum of the d areas is N Gamma. Since dim F=d-1,
the preceding simplex coupling has exactly this parameter a.

After normalizing facet area, the two full physical measures are

    mu=delta_0 X+sum_j delta_(p_j)X,
    nu=s delta_0 Y+lambda sum_j delta_(p_j)X,

where lambda=(N+1)/[N(1+Gamma)], s=lambda N Gamma, and
s-1=N(1-lambda). For d>=2, N Gamma>1, hence 0<lambda<1 and s>1.
Jensen across the base vertices at each fixed Y, followed by Y<=cx X
at each fixed base, gives nu<=cx mu for every joint convex physical
test. All coefficients have the stated signs. Thus no convex roof
test for this selected cover detects a descent.

The multiplier sum is N lambda=(N+1)/(1+Gamma)>1/Gamma.
Consequently the asserted per-group multiplier bound cannot follow
from these tests for one cover alone.

## 5. Actual descent and scope of the obstruction

Changing two outer radii to 1-s,1+s keeps their mean, and therefore
the central affine radius, equal to one. This is a positive affine
radius on the outer simplex for 0<s<=1/(4d), so it defines an actual
convex family. Its denominator is at least N+1. The central numerator
Gamma+(1-s)^d is strictly below Gamma+1, and the outer numerator is
at most Gamma exp(1/4)<(4/3)Gamma<Gamma+1. The exact radius formula
therefore proves strict descent.

Alternatively, a critical cover in which all caps include the same
outer fiber has a nonzero weighted base first moment on each shared
facet, while the full facet measure's base first moment is zero.
No normalized nonnegative multipliers can remove that mismatch.
This is why the universal quantifier over selected critical covers
rejects the example even though its balanced cover satisfies all
the convex-order tests.

The calculations preserve the source's precise limitation: a single
cover can pass all concave-roof tests at a nonminimum. The example is
OC-safe and does not refute conditions at a genuine unrestricted
minimum with the full universal-cover quantifier.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
